title: The Hollow's Own: An Independent's Home Ground

success_criteria.description: All three districts are in use and every precinct is assigned.
All three districts have roughly equal population (within 15%).

character.name: You
character.motivation: Two parties run across Hollowmere: the Ken Party out west and the Ryu Party through the central townships, each with a candidate in every district. But the eastern Hollow has its own — Dhalsim, an independent, no party behind him. His neighbours favour him right across the east, yet he stands in only one race: the district that holds his home. Where you draw the lines decides whether the Hollow gets a voice.

intro_slides.body: Dhalsim isn't a party — he's the Hollow's own. Out east he's the favourite, ahead of both Ken and Ryu on his home ground. But an independent runs where he lives: he appears on the ballot only in the district that contains his home, marked with a ⌂ pin on the map.
intro_slides.heading: An Independent's Home Ground

intro_slides.body: Switch to the Lean view and you'll see Dhalsim's teal spread across the east — that's who FAVOURS him. It isn't who can VOTE for him. Support that sits in a district which doesn't hold his home is support he can't collect: he isn't on that ballot. Lean is map-wide; the ballot is home-only.
intro_slides.heading: A Lean Is Not a Ballot

intro_slides.body: To send Dhalsim to the assembly, draw his home and enough of his eastern base into ONE district. Keep the Hollow together and he carries it. Split it across districts — or pull his home out into Ken's or Ryu's ground — and his neighbours' support scatters, uncounted, and a party takes the seat instead.
intro_slides.heading: Give the Hollow a Voice

narrative.objective: Draw three balanced, connected districts — a legal map, like before — and read the result. There's no seat to chase: keep Dhalsim's home (the ⌂ pin) and his eastern base together in one district and watch him carry the Hollow; crack it and his support scatters off his ballot. Can you draw a map that gives the Hollow a voice of its own?
narrative.epilogue: A home-base independent lives or dies by a single line. A party spreads its risk across many seats; an independent bets everything on the shape of one district — the one that holds his home. Keep a community together and it can elect its own; split it and its voice vanishes, even when a clear majority there favours them. The lines don't just divide the vote — they decide who is even allowed on the ballot.
